# `Q-22-3` — Mismatched Math Environment

> A math environment is closed by the wrong `\end{…}`, is never closed, or an `\end{…}` appears without its `\begin{…}`.

## What this means

`\begin{name}` and `\end{name}` must pair up exactly. When they do not, the extent of the environment is a guess, so quarto-math keeps the whole span verbatim rather than pick a layout that might be wrong, and reports the mismatch at the environment.

## Why this happens

Common causes: `\begin{aligned} … \end{align}` after editing one of the two, a missing `\end{…}` at the end of a display equation, or a stray `\end{…}` left behind after deleting a `\begin{…}`.

## How to fix it

Make the `\begin` and `\end` names identical and make sure every `\begin` has an `\end` inside the same `$$ … $$` block.

## Where it is reported

Math diagnostics point into the `.qmd` at the exact characters inside the
`$…$` or `$$…$$` block, including math that spans several lines or sits
inside a block quote or list item. When a `\newcommand` macro is involved,
a problem inside the macro body points at the definition and a problem in
a macro argument points at the use.
